semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {أَنْ أَنذِرْ}: It may be the explicative «أَنْ» (mufassira), or the maṣdar-forming one (maṣdariyya), that is: "We sent him with the warning." al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: We sent him by saying to him: «أَنْذِرْ» ("warn"), that is: We sent him with the command to warn." End of quotation. What he has implied is very good, and it is an answer to a question I raised earlier on this topic: namely that their statement "the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ» may be joined to the imperative" is problematic, because from it and what follows it a maṣdar is formed, and then the indication of the command is lost. Do you not see that if you imply, in «كَتَبْتُ إليه بأَنْ قُمْ», "I wrote to him standing", the indication of the command is lost at the very point where the command is stated explicitly? So it should be implied as al-Zamakhsharī said, that is: "I wrote to him by saying to him: «قُمْ»", that is, "I wrote to him with the command to stand."

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أَنِ اعبدوا}: It is either explicative (tafsīriyya) of «نذير», or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and the discussion of it is as given above for its sister.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ}: There are several views about this «مِنْ». First: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya). Second: that it marks the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). Third: that it is for clarifying the genus, which is rejected because nothing precedes it for it to clarify. Fourth: that it is redundant (zāʾida). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a Kufan view." I say: that is not their view, because they require only that its genitive noun be indefinite and require nothing else; and al-Akhfash requires nothing, so its redundancy here goes along with his view, not theirs.
His saying: {وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إلى أَجَلٍ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how does He say «ويُؤَخِّرْكم» when He informs that postponement of it is impossible? I say: Allah decreed that if the people of Noah believed, He would give them a life of a thousand years, and if they remained in their disbelief, He would destroy them at the head of nine hundred. So it was said to them: if you believe you will be given respite until the longer term; then He told them that when that furthest term comes it is not postponed." End of quotation. Those who speak of two terms have clung to this verse; the answer to that was given earlier. His saying: {لَوْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted, that is: "you would have hastened to what He commanded you."

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لِتَغْفِرَ}: It may be causal (lil-taʿlīl), the thing they were called to being omitted, that is: "I called them to believe in You for the sake of Your forgiving them"; or it may be the lām of transitivity (lām al-taʿdiya), in which case the cause is expressed by the effect, which is their being made so. The original is: "I called them to repentance, which is a cause of forgiveness." «جعلوا» is the governing word in «كلما», and it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنِّي».
His saying: {لَيْلاً وَنَهَاراً}: two adverbials of «دَعَوْت». What is meant is to report the continuity of the calling and that he did not slacken in it. «إلاَّ فِراراً» is a second object, and it is a "voided" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {جِهَاراً}: It may be a maṣdar in sense, since calling may be done openly or otherwise, so it falls under the category of «قَعَدَ القُرْفُصاءَ» ("he sat squatting"); or what is meant by «دَعَوْتُهم» is «جاهَرْتُهم» ("I addressed them openly"); or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "an open calling"; or it may be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "openly" or "possessing openness", or the maṣdar itself is made the ḥāl for emphasis. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: He mentioned that he called them night and day, then called them openly, then called them in secret and in public; so these must be three different callings for the conjunction to be sound? I say: he, peace be upon him, acted as one does who enjoins the right and forbids the wrong, beginning with the easier and then advancing to the harsher and harsher. So he began the counsel in secret; when they did not accept, he repeated with open address; when they did not accept, he made a third with a combination of secrecy and publicity. The meaning of «ثم» is to indicate the distance between the states, because open address is harsher than secrecy, and combining the two is harsher than either alone." The Shaykh said: "It has been repeated much by him that «ثُمَّ» expresses remoteness (istibʿād), and we do not know this from anyone else." I say: this statement, after you have heard al-Zamakhsharī's words, is an unfair attack on him.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {مِّدْرَاراً}: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماء». It is not made feminine because the form مِفْعال is not made feminine. One says: «امرأةٌ مئِنْاثٌ» ("a woman who bears many daughters") and «مِذْكار» ("who bears many sons"), and it takes the tāʾ only rarely, and then masculine and feminine are alike in it, so you say: «رجلٌ مِجْذامَةٌ ومِطْرابَةٌ» and «امرأة مِجْذامَةٌ ومِطْرابَةٌ». Or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a copious sending". The discussion of it was given in al-Anʿām.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَقَاراً}: It may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), with several senses. Among them: "What is the matter with you that you do not expect reverence (تَوْقيراً) for Him, that is, exaltation?" al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: What is the matter with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for Allah's exalting you in the abode of reward? And «لله» is a clarification of the one revered (al-muwaqqar); had it come later, it would have been a ṣila (connected complement)." End of quotation. That is: had «لله» come after «وَقارا», it would have been attached to it, so the reverence would be from them to Allah the Exalted, which is the opposite of the meaning he intended. Among them also: "You do not fear forbearance from Allah and His leaving off hastening the punishment, so that you would believe." Among them: "You do not fear greatness from Allah." On the first, the hope (rajāʾ) is in its proper sense; it has already been mentioned that its use in the sense of fear is figurative or shared. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تَرْجُون», that is: "revering Allah the Exalted," that is, exalting Him; then «للَّهِ» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «وَقارا», or the lām is redundant in the direct object, and two things make this fair here: that the governing word is derived (a secondary form), and that the governed word is put first. «لا تَرْجُون» is a ḥāl, and a parallel was given earlier in al-Māʾida.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya) from the agent of «تَرْجُون». الأَطْوار means the different states. The poet said:
4340 - فإنْ أفاقَ قد طارَتْ عَمَايَتُه ... والمَرْءُ يُخْلَقُ طَوْراً بعد أطوارِ
(If he recovers, his blindness has flown off; and man is created stage after stage.) It is accusative as ḥāl, that is: "passing from state to state," or "differing, between evildoer and doer of good, righteous and corrupt."

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {طِبَاقاً}: The discussion of it was given in Sūrat al-Mulk. Makkī said: "al-Farrāʾ permitted, outside the Qur'an, the genitive of «طباق» as an adjective of «سماوات»," meaning that it may be an adjective of the number at one time and of the counted noun at another.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {فِيهِنَّ}: that is, in the heavens, though the moon is in only one heaven of them. It was said: it is in the lowest heaven. This is allowed because there is contiguity between the heavens, so it is sound. One says "Zayd is in the city" when he is only in one corner of its corners.
His saying: {وَجَعَلَ الشمس سِرَاجاً}: The implied form may be: "and He placed the sun in them," as above. As for the sun, it was said: in the fourth heaven; it was said: in the fifth; it was said: in winter in the fourth and in summer in the seventh. Allah knows best which of these is correct.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {نَبَاتاً}: It is either a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَنْبَتَ» with the augment letters dropped, called ism maṣdar, or it is governed by an implied «نَبَتُّمْ», that is: "so you grew a growth," so that it is accusative by the implied intransitive form. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or it is accusative by «أَنْبَتكم», because it includes the meaning of «نَبَتُّمْ»." The Shaykh said: "I cannot make sense of this second view." I say: this view is the one I gave earlier, namely that it is accusative by «أَنْبَتكم» with the augment letters dropped. The meaning of his saying "because it includes the meaning of «نَبَتُّمْ»" is that it contains it; the most that is in it is that its augments were dropped. The "causing to grow" here is an eloquent metaphor.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً}: In al-Anbiyāʾ «الفِجاجُ» was put first, to harmonise the verse endings here. Something like this has already been discussed.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {وَوَلَدُهُ}: The disagreement of the readers about «وَلَدِه» has been given, and it was mentioned that they are two dialectal forms, like بُخْل and بَخَل. Abū Ḥātim said: it is possible that the form with ḍamma is the plural of the form with fatḥa, like خَشَب and خُشْب. He recited for Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him:
4341 - يا بِكرَ آمنةَ المباركَ وِلْدُها ... مِنْ وُلْدِ مُحْصَنَةٍ بسَعْدٍ الأَسْعُدِ
(O firstborn of Āmina, whose children are blessed, of the children of a chaste woman, with the luckiest of fortunes.)

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَمَكَرُواْ}: It is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ». The pronoun is plural only by being carried over to the sense, after being carried over to the form of the word in {لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ}. It may also be a fresh sentence, informing about the unbelievers.
His saying: {كُبَّاراً}: The majority read it with ḍamma on the kāf and shadda on the bāʾ, a form of intensification stronger than «كُبار» with ḍamma and light bāʾ. ʿĪsā said: it is a Yemeni dialect, and he recited:
4342 - والمرءُ يُلْحِقُه بفِتيان النَّدى ... خُلُقُ الكريمِ وليس بالوُضَّاء
(A man is brought into the company of the youths of generosity by the character of the noble, not by being handsome.) And the words of another:
4343 - بَيْضاءُ تصطادُ القلوبَ وتَسْتَبي ... بالحسنِ قلبَ المسلمِ القُرَّاء
(A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates with beauty the heart of the Muslim, the reciter.) One says: «رجلٌ طُوَّالٌ وحُمَّالٌ وحُسَّانٌ». ʿĪsā, Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with ḍamma and a light bāʾ, which is also a form of intensification but less than the first. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Muḥayṣin also read it with kasra on the kāf and a light bāʾ. Abū Bakr said: it is the plural of «كبير», as though he made «مَكْراً» stand in place of «ذنوب» or «أفاعيل», meaning that is why he described it with a plural.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تَذَرُنَّ وَدّاً وَلاَ سُوَاعاً}: It may be an instance of conjoining the particular to the general (ʿaṭf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm) if it is said that these names are of idols, and it may not be so if it is said that they are names of righteous men, as mentioned in the exegesis. Nāfiʿ read «وُدّاً» with ḍamma on the wāw, and the rest with fatḥa. The words of the poet were recited with both forms:
4344 - حَيَّاكَ وَدٌّ فإنَّا لا يَحِلُّ لنا ... لَهْوُ النساءِ وإنَّ الدين قد عزما
(May Wadd greet you; for we are not permitted the amusement of women, and religion has become resolute.) And the words of another:
4345 - فحيَّاكِ وَدٌّ مِنْ هُداكِ لفِتْيَةٍ ... وخُوْصٍ بأعلى ذي فُضالةَ مُنْجِدِ
(May Wadd greet you, from your guidance, for young men and hollow-eyed camels on the heights of Dhū Fuḍāla, going to the highlands.)
His saying: {وَلاَ يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ}: The majority read both without tanwīn. If they are Arabic, the prohibition of the ṣarf (the diptote status) is because of being proper names and the verb pattern; if they are non-Arabic, it is because of being proper names and foreignness. al-Aʿmash read «ولا يَغُوْثاً ويَعُوْقاً», declined with tanwīn. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is a slip, because definiteness is inherent and the verb pattern is present." End of quotation.
It is not a slip, for two reasons. One: that he made them fully declinable for harmony, since before them there are two declinable names and after them a declinable name, just as «سلاسل» was made declinable. The other: that it follows the dialect of those who make the diptote declinable in every case, a dialect related by al-Kisāʾī.
Abū al-Faḍl transmitted the declension of both from al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, then said: "He made them of the pattern فَعُول, so he declined them; as for the majority, they are two adjectives from الغَوْث and العَوْق." I say: this is problematic speech. As for his saying «فَعُولاً», it is not correct, since the roots «يغث» and «يعق» are non-existent. As for his saying "two adjectives from الغَوْث and العَوْق," there is no «يَفْعُل» among adjectives or nouns, and the correct view is what I gave earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is a problematic reading, because whether they are Arabic or non-Arabic, they are diptotes; perhaps he intended the pairing (izdiwāj) and so declined them, finding their sisters declinable: وَدّاً, سُوعاً and نَسْراً." The Shaykh said: "It is as though he was not aware that declining what is a diptote is a dialect."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {وَقَدْ أَضَلُّواْ}: that is, the leaders, or the idols; and He gathered them in the plural of rational beings, treating them as rational beings are treated.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَزِدِ}: It is conjoined to His saying: {رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي} [Nūḥ: 21], by way of reporting Noah's speech after «قال» and after the wāw that stands in its place, that is: "He said: 'they disobeyed me,' and said: 'do not increase,'" that is, he said these two sayings, so both are in the position of the accusative. This was said by al-Zamakhsharī. He said: "As you say: «قال زيدٌ: نوديَ للصلاة وصَلِّ في المسجدِ»," reporting his two sayings with one conjoined to the other. The Shaykh said: "«ولا تَزِدْ» is conjoined to «قد أَضَلُّوا», because they are reported by an implied «قال», and correspondence is not required among conjoined clauses; one may conjoin a statement to a request and the reverse, contrary to those who required it."

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِّمَّا خطيائاتهم}: «ما» is redundant between the preposition and its genitive noun, for emphasis. Whoever does not hold it redundant makes it indefinite and makes «خطيئاتِهم» a badal (substitute), which involves arbitrary forcing. The disagreement about the reading of «خَطِيْئاتِهم» was given in al-Aʿrāf. Abū Rajāʾ read «خَطِيَّاتهم» as a sound plural, except that he assimilated the yāʾ into the yāʾ that had been changed from the hamza. al-Jaḥdarī, and it is also transmitted from Ubayy, read «خطيئتِهم» in the singular with hamza. ʿAbd Allāh read «مِنْ خطيئاتِهم ما أُغْرِقوا», placing the redundant «ما» between the verb and what is attached to it. «مِنْ» is causal and is attached to «أُغْرِقوا». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "it marks the beginning of the range," which is not clear. The majority read «أُغرِقوا» from «أَغْرق». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «غُرِّقوا» with shadda; both are for making transitive. One says: «أغرَقْتُ زيداً في الماء» and «غَرَّقْتُه فيه».
His saying: {فَأُدْخِلُواْ}: it may be an expression of the future by the past, because its occurrence is certain, like {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]; or it may be in its proper sense, what is meant being their being exposed to the Fire in their graves, as He says of the family of Pharaoh: {النار يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً} [Ghāfir: 46].

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {دَيَّاراً}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "دَيَّار is among the nouns used in general negation. One says «ما بالدار دَيَّارٌ ودَيُّورٌ» ("there is no one at all in the house"), like قَيَّام and قَيُّوم. It is of the pattern فَيْعال from الدُّور or from الدار. Its origin is دَيْوار, and what is done to the origin of سَيِّد and مَيِّت was done to it; had it been فَعَّال, it would have been دَوَّاراً." End of quotation. He means that its wāw should have remained sound and not been changed to yāʾ. This is similar to the discussion he gave earlier of «متحيِّز», that its origin is مُتَحَيْوِز, of the pattern مُتَفَيْعِل, not مُتَفَعِّل, since otherwise it would have had to be مُتَحَوِّزاً, because it is from الحَوْز. It is also said in it دَوَّار, like قَيَّام and قَوَّام.
Makkī said: "Its origin is دَيْوار, then they assimilated the wāw into the yāʾ, like «مَيِّت», whose origin is مَيْوِت, then they assimilated the second into the first. It is also possible that they changed the wāw into yāʾ, then assimilated the first yāʾ into the second." I say: his saying "they assimilated the second into the first" is not permissible, since the established rule for two close letters is to change the first to the second, and the reverse is not allowed except as an anomaly or by a morphological necessity. As for the anomaly, it is like the reading «واذكر» [Yūsuf: 45] with dhāl and «فَهَلْ مِن مُّذَّكِرٍ» [al-Qamar: 15], also with dhāl; its investigation has already been given. As for the morphological necessity, it is like «امدحْ هِلالاً», with the hāʾ changed to ḥāʾ so that the stronger is not assimilated into the weaker; this is known to one who has worked in morphology (taṣrīf).

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {رَّبِّ اغفر لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ}: The majority read the dāl with fatḥa, as the dual of «والِد», meaning his two parents. al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur and al-Nakhaʿī read «ولوَلَدَيَّ», the dual of «وَلَد», meaning his two sons Sām and Ḥām. Ibn Jubayr and al-Jaḥdarī read «ولوالِدِيْ» with kasra on the dāl, meaning his father. It is possible that he meant his nearest father, who begot him, and singled him out for mention because he is more honourable than the mother; or that he meant all who begot him, from Adam, peace be upon him, down to the one who begot him. «مؤمناً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «تَباراً» is a second object; and the exception is a "voided" one (istithnāʾ mufarragh). التبار means destruction, and its origin is from breaking and crumbling. The investigation of that has already been given, and to Allah belong praise and favour.
